text: The relationship between EI and conscientiousness reflects a complex connection, where an individual’s ability to understand, manage, and effectively utilize their emotional states is intricately linked to conscientiousness ( Szcześniak et al., 2020 ). Although EI has been widely studied in general sports psychology, research on the unique psychological challenges faced by Paralympic athletes remains limited. In this context, understanding the role of conscientiousness within EI for this population may offer valuable insights into their psychological resilience. EI encompasses the ability to recognize, express, understand, and manage emotions ( Goleman, 2017 ), while conscientiousness involves the skills of control, organization, and stability to achieve long-term goals ( Somer et al., 2002 ).
source_label: Unveiling the associations between conscientiousness and emotional intelligence in Paralympic athletes
